full_judgment:
4. Mr. Md. Ibrahim Khalil, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Court of Appeal below and the High Court Division committed an error of law resulting error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in overlooking the oral and documentary evidence on record proving their case and observing, inter-alia, that that the defendant Nos. 1, 3-4 did not adduce any evidence to prove their case. The learned Advocate-on-Record further submitted that it was Tanu Miah who was the real owner of 3:37 acres of land of suit Khatian being bereft of the consideration of host of oral and documentary evidence on record proving that it was Haji Kala Miah who was the real owner of the entire land of suit Khatian and the same was inherited by his heirs long before the disputed mortgage by Tanu Miah and auction purchase by Abdul Huq Bepari; that the suit for partition simple without any prayer for declaration of title was not maintainable. 

 5. It appears that Tanu Miah was the owner of the suit lands who had mort-gaged the same to Abdul Huq Bepari and in execution of a decree, Abdul Huq Bepari purchased the suit lands through Court. Subsequently, Abdul Hug Bepari by different deeds transferred the suit lands to the plaintiff and the defendants other than the defendant Nos. 1, 3 and 4. The heirs of Kala Miah never challenged the title of farm Miah or Abdul Huq Bepari at any point of time. `Farm Miah alone exercised his title in the suit lands and the C.S. Khatian was prepared in his name. Tanu Miah as exclusive owner mortgaged the suit lands with Abdul Huq Bepari. It appears that neither 'farm Miah's title nor Abdul Huq Bepari's title was disputed at any point of time. It is more than 60 years after exercising such title and possession, the defendants came up with a case that the lands were wrongly recorded in the name of Tanu Miah and disputed about title of Tanu Miah, ' although Tanu Miah's title was extinguished in 1931 and Abdul Huq Bepari by dint of a decree passed by a Court of law ex-erased his exclusive right and title in the suit lands.
